steps.title: Portrait mode for your profile picture
steps.body: Portrait mode (often a small head icon) blurs the background while keeping you in sharp focus — just like a real camera lens. Perfect for a profile picture that stands out.

steps.title: Burst mode for that one perfect shot
steps.body: Hold down the shutter button (or swipe it left/right) to quickly take several photos in a row. Essential for a group of friends jumping, or a pet that won't sit still — you pick the best one from the series afterward.

steps.title: Panorama for festival or travel photos
steps.body: Choose panorama mode to capture a wide landscape or a packed festival crowd in a single photo. Turn slowly in a circle while your phone stitches the photos together.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Try taking a portrait photo and a panorama photo.

lessons.title: Quick editing for Instagram and TikTok

steps.title: Built-in editing tools
steps.body: Every Photos app has basic editing: cropping, filters, and sliders for light, contrast, and saturation. Start here before downloading a separate app.

steps.title: More control with an app
steps.body: Want more? Apps like Snapseed (free), or the editing tools built into Instagram/TikTok themselves, give finer control: selectively adjust part of a photo, remove distracting details, fine-tune sharpness.

steps.title: Don't overdo the filters
steps.body: A small adjustment to light and contrast often already makes a big difference. Too many filters, smoothing, or overly bright colors can make a photo look unnatural or fake — and people spot that pretty fast these days.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Edit a photo from your gallery: adjust the light and contrast, and compare it to the original.

lessons.title: Editing videos for Reels and TikTok

steps.title: Trimming a video
steps.body: Open a video in your Photos app and tap 'Edit'. Drag the handles at the start and end of the timeline inward to cut off the unnecessary part.

steps.title: Combining clips and cutting fast
steps.body: For a Reel or TikTok, use an app like CapCut — drag clips into order, cut to the beat of the music, and add text or transitions without expensive software.

steps.title: Music and volume levels
steps.body: In the same editor you can usually add a music track under your video. Watch the volume level: the music shouldn't drown out voices in your video, and check copyrighted music — platforms like TikTok/Instagram usually offer a built-in, licensed music library.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Trim a video down to the most important part, then share it with someone.

steps.title: Automatic backup
steps.body: Make sure your photos automatically upload to the cloud (Google Photos or iCloud), so you never lose your memories if your phone breaks, gets stolen, or you lose it at a festival. Turn this on once in the settings.

steps.title: Sharing a link instead of dozens of separate photos
steps.body: Sharing a lot of photos from a night out or a trip? Send a share link to an album, instead of dozens of separate photos in the group chat. Faster and clearer for everyone.

steps.title: Setting permissions on a shared album
steps.body: With a shared album you can often choose whether others can also add photos — handy for a festival, holiday, or party where everyone's taking pictures and you want it all in one place.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Check whether automatic backup is turned on on your phone, and create a shared album for a group of friends or family.
